# The Book of the King’s Face
<note>Hebrew: Sefer Pnei Melekh. This title likely refers to the Divine Presence or the countenance of a sovereign.</note>

And I, the humble Isaac, son of the house of those who preceded me, the least of the scribes in the life of the resurrection of the dead; and from there my name is written, and my hand succeeded with good fortune and suc<unclear>cess</unclear>. And good is His Name, blessed above all blessing and praise, He who guides; and He brought me by His hand to write. And the merit is mine and that of the holy and awesome congregation, to ascend to the City of the King, the chosen one which was of old, **Mount Gerizim**. <note>The sacred mountain of the Samaritans.</note> And I desired again with love, and with a heart and purity of grace and sweetness. I wrote by the grace of the Most High, and I sanctified the vessel and the throne for the spices of the sources of the fields, upon the planting where my portion lies. And may those who preceded the return of the passerby and the traveler be found worthy. And let no man’s dreams wear me out; let [this work] stand firm and not depart, for I trust in the strong ones. It is full and wide and fixed and supported by Him, to uphold all bonds and to leave over the remnants of the city of lips <note>A poetic reference to prayer or speech.</note>, simple so-and-so, and written completely, and in time, and pleasant and diligent. And may the Holy One arise—peace, peace in joy—and may fear and distress not rule in my dwelling. And may he who is of high degree hasten and write for him; and even so, let it not be a small thing in the eyes of the one who took pity, for he was my son, my very presence, a bond for a memorial of the miracle of grace and kindness. And at first I intended to say: the "Kindness of the King" <note>Hebrew: Hesed Melekh</note> is the Guide, the bestower of kindnesses; and He sent to him the horn in which the Holy One, Blessed be He, <note>A translation of the Aramaic/Hebrew "Kudsha Brich Hu," a common title for God.</note> His ancient ones and His hosts, and the one who makes His paths good, and the heights of the abundance of the fields of good intellect to bind up, and a vessel to fill the pious one in his soul. And may he rejoice in their building, and especially Solomon the King who preceded me; lean upon them and write for them, Amen.

# The Book of Life and Holiness

In this book of life, before the Holy One <note>original: "Kadosh"</note>, I have ascended to their heights.
A complete composition <term>Chibur: a formal rabbinic work or treatise</term> written in its day and time, leaning upon the high fortress by His permission and grace.
The oaths are presented with offerings and sweet saturation, a law <note>original: "nimus," often referring to social or natural law</note> from the mouth of a scribe written in a book.
Good is the reputation of the signs of the chapters and the established laws <note>original: "dinim"</note> which were extracted from the skin of Sodom <note>A metaphorical reference to harsh or wicked origins being transformed through justice</note>.
In righteousness, he joins Enoch <note>The biblical figure Enoch, often associated in mystical literature with the recording of heavenly secrets</note> and their commandments, which bound grace and His kindness.
And he planted the ancient root, while the wicked are trampled by those wearing the vision they have forged.
The desire of his vision was drawn to their garment, and they separated a portion of the strength of Joshua <note>original: "Yehoshua"</note>.
Lest their vision be hidden; for they sinned in transgression, yet the merit of the transgression plucks away the lack here.
They sinned for themselves, and in the thread of their deeds they abandoned, and they honored and sought a revealed vision.
The mouth of their vision was snared, and to add to the soul, he shall also strengthen the bond of grace over transgression.
In its source, merit is kindness and heart, and the princes; and he has knowledge of the transgression now.
They lived in transgression and lacked nothing, yet they have a lack; and the man of the cold shall support us.
Grace and sight, and when his refuge is established and they answered; and they turned their faces if they should be completed.
Pure and sparing of grace, his grace and clean; they inclined their mouths to precede, and he has salvation.
And upon the kindness of the source and the vision of his overseer, etc. The peace-offerings and the desire of the openings.
They returned to grace, and in kindness the wicked, the sons of Isaac <note>original: "Yitzhak"</note>, desired the wicked and the silence of the wicked.
And the clean hypocrite stirred to seek kindness, and he strengthened the wicked and the lack.
His wrath ruled, and the silence and the multitude of voices—they tasted it—and the majority to investigate, to strengthen, and to turn away.
The living being desired and sought for the hope of its mouth, and it abandoned and was in the gate of grace.
He erased transgression; grace favored us in kindness; the lack preceded us, and the vision of the one who carries it.
And strengthen and show them favor; and the request found a solution, and the vision shall break, and the kindness of their heart is fear.
Open your face, and the groups of their thoughts and their attainment you have envisioned; and the vision of His kindness.
Grace for their sin they called, and kindness is a tablet in the vision, and the destruction and sacrifice of transgression.

Some of the preliminary knowledge: and behold, when all the wise-hearted <term>Chachmei Lev: a biblical term for those endowed with divine skill, here referring to master scholars</term> and their peers were present, and after the wisdoms of the Torah rested upon them, they dealt with absolute contradictions and the gathering of opposites. They weighed the matter of judgment and the distinctions between them, asking what constitutes a deficiency and what constitutes a merit, and whether knowledge precedes action. After this, they considered certain types of knowledge that are not perceived by the senses. This knowledge, through which we have grasped the final foundation, underwent a change of will before the Lord to be revealed. This strengthened the matter of the **Secret of Absolute Seclusion** <note>original: "Sod HaHesger HaMuchlat," likely referring to a mystical concept of divine withdrawal or the hidden nature of God's essence</note>, including its contradictions in both general and particular terms, and it established the agreed-upon truth among the holy ones and our Sages of Blessed Memory <note>Hebrew: "Razal"</note>. 

For this aforementioned reason, I desired to explain some of the path to bring strength and fortitude to the faith in the Lord, may He be blessed, and to understand the words of the great Torah scholars in their positions. They were the ones who guided the spiritual standings through their exalted wisdom, for which there is no aid to be found in the books currently available to us. For those who hear them and those who see the Lord, much is missing from them—each one regarding the laws and the secrets of the Torah and the commandments intended for people of faith. This is so that they may remove the heart of those who are lacking, and to provide strength at a boundary far removed from the sect of deniers <note>referring to those who deny providence or the validity of the Torah</note>. Thus, these truths shall be placed in their hearts in such a measure that they will not enter or be hidden in the error of doubt.

## Chapter One

Regarding the examination of the Blessed One, as He is called in our Torah: He is **self-sufficient** <note>literally "rich in His soul," meaning God lacks nothing and requires nothing external</note>. He possesses this verse and the contradiction of its vision, serving as an absolute intellectual salvation. For it would be wicked to say that the Blessed One's state of "wealth" or existence would depart simply because He has a desire for the creature <note>the created being</note> whose life was spared through that knowledge and in His memory. This "innovation" or "novelty" <term>Chiddush: the act of bringing something new into being</term> arises from the side of the necessity for which His will was enacted. We do not say that these are drawn from two different sides, but rather it is accepted from the perspective of the "rectification" <term>Tikun: the process of mending or restoring the spiritual world</term> which returned and strengthened the presence before Him. This return was not "burnt out" from this side, standing instead in a slight change of the **Divine Overflow** <term>Shefa: the spiritual influence or energy emanating from God to the world</term>. Since this is not a will for its own sake, it is known that the deficiency within the "lack of wealth" <note>referring again to the concept of God's self-sufficiency versus the perceived "need" to create</note> exists only in human thought.

<summary>This page introduces a theological defense of faith, focusing on resolving contradictions in Torah wisdom and explaining the "Secret of Absolute Seclusion." Chapter One begins an inquiry into God's self-sufficiency, arguing that God's desire to create does not imply a deficiency in His divine essence.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the philosophical inquiry from the previous section. While the previous page established the "Secret of Seclusion" and the foundations of faith, this page transitions into the practical application of these ideas through prayer, the study of Torah, and the "nature of the lamps," likely a metaphor for divine illumination. It introduces the "Fourth Action" and prepares the reader for the specific insights of Chapter Three.</meta>

This booklet <term>Kuntres: a term for a small manuscript, pamphlet, or scholarly treatise</term> investigates that which is missing and will greatly resolve [the mysteries of] the Divine Name <note>original: "Y-H," the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>, existence itself, and the general principles of the holiness of prayer. It encompasses all the heavens, foreign tongues, and the "apples" <note>likely a reference to the "Field of Holy Apples," a Kabbalistic metaphor for the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>, and a prayer that one should value greatly. Its beginning is to write clear intellectual insights, and then it binds the majestic connection of the matter: namely, that all deeds, customs, and obligations, and the spiritual sensitivity that flows from them, shall live and be sustained. 

Even the ancients who dwelt in cities were once unable to receive their "morsel of bread" <note>a metaphor for basic spiritual sustenance or fundamental Torah knowledge</note>. To them, he shall open the innovations of the Holy Torah and the clear teaching <term>Mishnah Berurah: literally "clarified teaching," here likely referring to the pursuit of clear halakhic or philosophical understanding</term> throughout most of the day and night. He opens for them the "horn of plenty" <note>original: "Keren Mosaf," implying an increase in spiritual capital or merit</note>, and its richness is visible to our distant eyes—between one meal and the next—rising above the errors and logical analogies that were concluded in the establishment of this composition. From it, one may understand how to join the ranks of the Pious <term>Chassidim: those who go beyond the letter of the law in their devotion</term>, whose deeds and actions are precious.

Among the many songs associated with His name, there is reason and grace for all these creatures. Through a holy mind, he possesses a vision amidst wanderings <note>original: "Nidot," which can also refer to the laws of purity, but here suggests a state of exile or movement</note>, a vision for life. This is for the "blessed upon the blessed" at the gateway, to bring life or to uproot. Even Joseph the Dark One <note>original: "Yosef HaKedar," possibly a pseudonym or a reference to a specific historical figure known to the author</note> earned his reward. The three "Living Creatures" <note>original: "Chayyot," referring to the angelic beings in Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</note> are all before him in this place, regarding the existence of the sinner; and the general life-force of the world flows from the man to the layman. 

What emerges from this "good passage" is the health of the hearts implanted within him. His insight <note>original: "Ta'amo," literally "his taste" or "his reasoning"</note> has spread outward, and they supported him from below in the matters of the Pious and their dealings. These possessions—the Five Books of the Torah and the twenty-four books of Scripture—are our guardians. This is the "General Vision," and this is the "Fourth Action" wherein he toils and requires divine contemplation regarding the "Living Creatures." The interpretation can rise like a rose <note>original: "Shushan," also referring to the city of Susa</note> higher than what remained in this place, lest He enlighten my eyes through the "planting of kindness" to utter a song of strength.

<meta>This page transitions from the general spiritual obligations discussed previously into a technical philosophical and mystical analysis of the "Active Intellect" and its relationship to the natural world. Bound arrangements above the circle; let him guard his soul and instruct within a portion of the space. All that is hidden is the golden planting <note>original: "katom," which can mean orange or fine gold; likely a reference to a mystical orchard or divine emanation</note>. When reading the prophecies according to this [planting], he shall know; it shall be gradual and in its illumination. Let him contemplate: is it from these [divine] hands that the testimony of the known miracles comes?

The ancients at the beginning of days—had he deduced from his own words—found that science <term>Mada: in this context, refers to rational inquiry or secular knowledge as opposed to prophecy</term> and nature stand in a state of flux <note>literally "in exchange"</note>, neither increasing nor truly existing in truth. Why are the heavens eternal? For he did not know that the Holy Intellect does not possess all the sciences, and its explanation alone is absolute for him. These are his testimony, and another [reason] is its flavor and its rest. 

The Active Intellect <term>Sekhel HaPoel: in medieval philosophy, the bridge between the divine mind and human reason</term> operates according to science. By turning their wisdom, these became for him the testimony of the intellect which he shall attain. The order is clear: all of nature is like a point on a surface. Even a simple man might ask: "What is it?" The connection has been clarified.

If the circumference be five—the measure of a man—and if there be a grace smaller than it, ten [is the measure]. The attributes <term>Middot: refers to both divine emanations and moral measurements</term> shall change more than is preferred. According to the circle that encompasses, there is that which precedes and that which follows. Since the exposition <term>Midrash: a method of interpretation or an homiletic teaching</term> of the ancients contains their reasons, they are the law of the year. The internal connection [remains] sealed within the intellect.

The connection is the aspect of the testimony of the scientific intellect, upon which it is built; through this, they prove it. Now we shall explain: I have heard that it shall testify, and others will add to it. Outside of it, much labor shall increase in understanding. We do not know of any greater intellectual [attainment] than this in actual practice. For him, the individual is weighed as sixty <note>The number sixty often represents a "complete" or "nullifying" measure in Jewish thought</note>. Outside of what is understood, His Name stands [firm]. You shall explain secrets through points <note>Likely referring to the vowel points of the Hebrew alphabet or geometric points in a diagram</note>.

He shall change ten with forty-nine <note>Possibly a reference to the 49 Gates of Understanding</note>. The absolute connection from the side of the action, and the explanation of the encompassing inquiry, is a ladder. A flood <note>original: "shatzef," a sudden burst of water or wrath</note> shall be encompassed within it; it shall lengthen for the fifth understanding. Therefore, the attained concept <term>Musag: a philosophical term for a grasped idea or perceived truth</term> is known. Attain with Him; he shall attain through Him a complete understanding. Those who ask and respond concerning the secret of all things shall attain it. Existence is like a rock <note>original: "tzur," a common epithet for God as the "Rock" or "Fortress"</note> in the testimony of God. The mind cannot measure them. 

The structure is hushed at its root. The singular Rabbi <note>likely referring to Maimonides, known as the "Great Rabbi"</note> said that in his perfection he would find [the truth], for these things shall separate. This is the "Bonder" from the perspective of the Guide <note>original: "HaMoreh," almost certainly referring to Maimonides' *Guide for the Perplexed*</note>, and it concerns the precision of the lines, etc.

<meta>This page continues the transition from the previous discussion of "Active Intellect" into a deeper exploration of how the Creator’s "Simple Intellect" interacts with the individual through the mechanisms of Providence and Prophecy. It maintains the philosophical-mystical tone, focusing on the stripping away of materiality to reach intellectual union.</meta>

The **Creator**, may He be exalted, is ever-present through the power of the universal and the particular. His radiance <note>original: "Zohar," referring to a divine brilliance or the foundational mystical text</note> ascends, and there is never a moment of His absence. He is the **Simple Intellect** <term>Sekhel HaPashut: a philosophical term for the pure, non-composite divine mind</term> and the complete vitality; this is the essence of the matter.

There exists a certain relationship from which a fixed and known principle is drawn. For if it were so—falling below the heart of the one who is "precise" with man <note>referring to the divine quality of strict judgment or scrutiny of human actions</note>—one who possesses accompaniment and time. Behold, for him, death is according to the nature of his making, and the subtle forces within the Divine. He explained that from within the order of **Providence** <term>Hashgacha: divine supervision over the world and individuals</term>, it is spoken of in the **Attribute of Mercy**. This is what is called "Logic" or "Reasoning" <note>original: "Hegayon," referring here to the divine logic or logos underpinning creation</note>.

Therefore, all the goodness of the emanation—even if it is by my own will—is a balanced and intellectual matter arising from "Guidance." Concerning this difficult matter, it was attained in the form of the "Fear of Truth." Within the Divine, this person trembled and yearned for his world and his peace. Very much after this precision of the intellect, there is no weight or measure where the action exceeds the difficulty. In the holy work...

...smoke <note>original: "ashan," which can also be an acronym in Jewish mysticism for World (Olam), Year (Shanah), and Soul (Nefesh)</note>, for there the foundational elements will be tested. From there, the intermediary will arise and increase from the mouth or the defined voice following the other. This is the **Holy Name**.

Through the power of its instruction and its secret, one understands the mysteries of Isaac or Joseph and the cycle of the "End" <note>likely referring to the messianic era or the limits of prophetic time</note>. These prophetic insights are a prophecy for all; his "good setting" <note>referring to a spiritual descent or the setting of a heavenly body</note> comes from the foundation of the "plain." From his house, as he is solitary and lives in the "second" <note>perhaps the second stage of emanation or the second sphere</note> and stands firm.

The correct ones, who are accustomed to the "clouds" <note>a metaphor for divine veils or high spiritual states</note>, say that this is a simple, holy matter. Let him understand and be impressed: nothing exists in the senses except that its nature is balanced, just as the nature of the path of His **Providence** and His grace. This is not a path of loss for any creature. For example, one does not speak of the "secret" of the intellect's word, yet he will understand the intellect more in relation to the value of things. Its existence comes from **Kabbalah** <term>literally "reception" or "tradition," referring here to received mystical wisdom or the mystical system itself</term> outside of itself.

The intellect shall receive the **Simple Intellect**, its own understanding being drawn along with the secrets of the heart. Man exists on "that day," and he strips away the material to become a single essence: the very substance of the intellect. Behold the individual who received everything—even though it was the reception of the heart and understanding within the **Active Intellect** <term>Sekhel HaPoel: in medieval philosophy, the bridge between the human mind and the divine</term> which exists eternally. In it, the longing mind perceives, and he gains a perspective from the **Kabbalah** of the **General Intellect**.

### On the Types of Sustenance

**The types of food** and all the components of food—those that are beneficial and those that are harmful—have two sides. While some have a "bad foundation," others can actually improve health if eaten correctly. The food that provides nourishment yet causes the production of **humors** <term>HaMoriyot: based on the Galenic medical theory of the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which determine health and temperament</term> does so according to the nature of the food itself. 

Improper diet can lead to low spirits, the destruction of the body's strength, and the "thinning" of the brain <note>In this context, "thinning" likely refers to a weakening of intellectual capacity or a lack of mental substance</note>. It further corrupts the intellect and memory. Examples of such harmful foods include various fruits and vegetables—specifically **unripe fruits** <note>original: "pagim"</note> such as wild forest berries or fruits from young trees, and bitter herbs. These are most harmful when cooked. Conversely, vegetables that are mild or tasteless, and fruits that have fully ripened and "sealed" their growth, contain both pleasure and a hidden danger. 

(For all these foods draw [fluids] from the lungs, like **impurities** <note>possibly referring to "muddiness" or congestive fluids</note> and "bad waters.") 

Even if one’s individual nature is generally stable, these foods do not sustain the body's "nest" <note>a metaphor for the physical frame</note> but rather add a sting that can trouble the soul forever. However, food that tends toward the "good and beautiful" refined matter—such as high-quality wine, fish, and **choice wheat**—is different. When one consumes food with a good, sweet taste alongside these items, they will be nourished in health.

Fear for the body is best managed through constant care. If one moves through the year with good habits, their strength will remain. This all comes from **nutritional** <term>HaTizuni: relating to the faculty of growth and physical sustenance</term> perfection. When the body is held as something "precious," one will not require medicine. Seeking the "hidden good" of peace and health leads to a restful state. 

Some food passes through having caused harm, while other food acts as a bridge to health. Its nature is to be a "good transition," being strong enough that it does not succumb to change or decay. This is how the perfection of the body is achieved among those who do not suffer from weakness. 

After one has finished examining the body's needs in every matter, and uses their **intellect and understanding** for this high purpose, they have effectively "acquired" their body. Even if they fall into illness where their strength is low, they will know what is good for them—specifically, avoiding what is unnecessary. # Chapter 22

In this chapter are the reward and the punishment, and the matter therein is that every single person from among humankind should know that the Creator, may He be blessed, is the One who knows and observes and encompasses the conceived, the hidden, and the revealed <note>The author emphasizes Divine omniscience—God's ability to see into the most private parts of the human mind.</note> in every subtle and second detail. In His hand are the rest of man's affairs, so that strange and harmful thoughts should not arise in his heart. And He alone shall be within him, the Knower of his thoughts, while the intellect lives for his soul through them and in Him; for He is the One who observes and examines the hidden things and the wonders, beyond what any person has understood.

Regarding this matter—behold, it should not arise in his heart to speak of these things and their foundations <note>original: *arsheihen*; referring to the underlying supports or origins of these thoughts</note>, lest he abandon his protection in the world and occupy himself with the ways of the invalid and toward sin, and in the corruption of the knowledge of the Good. This is for one who does not understand the knowledge of the supreme and awesome Truth. And there is no way from the side of logic <note>original: *sevara*; a term often used in Talmudic reasoning to denote logical deduction as opposed to received tradition</note> that he should think. And when He speaks with him, his will desires the custom following this Good. He Himself is the value that enters his soul, for behold, to Him belong the thoughts and the will in his coming and in his honor.

For he knows, and the argument is beautiful, when the Truth exists while he occupies himself with this chapter, like one who lives with the awareness that the scripture was not meant simply. One should not transgress this, nor will it come to a man who knows the time and its seasons, the unique one in the depths of the orders of the Covenant <note>original: *Berit*; likely referring to the mystical "Covenant of the Word" or the "Covenant of the Flesh."</note> created for the Lord to supervise <note>original: *lehashgiach*; the root of *Hashgacha*, or Divine Providence, the idea that God actively intervenes in the world</note>. Within it is the **Secret of Creation** <note>original: *Sod ha-Beriah*; the esoteric knowledge of how the universe was formed</note>, and the yearning, and the Providence. Its hidden depths shall be revealed to itself, and the sound of the Shofar <note>The ram's horn, used here as a mystical symbol of awakening or Divine emanation.</note> that arrives because of the order of emergence <note>original: *balut*; can refer to a bud or the act of something emerging from concealment</note>. And it is the **Secret of His Name** <note>original: *Sod Shemo*</note> bound in a deep secret and a hidden order of things.

There is in this a great secret of the sanctities, and through it the wise shall understand the Torah in truth and the Good. They shall say of this that he composed it in our time, and from every body and thing in its breaking. For he stood, and behold, ten years of the decade—a decade—and he shall teach the remainder. And there came month by month, in its purity, a point and light <note>original: *hud ve-nahor*; a mystical phrase referring to sharp mental clarity and Divine illumination</note> of years and days, and all that is within its interior. # Chapter 8

## Chapter 18

An explanation of what is intended by the words of the prophet: **Approach** <note>original: "karav"</note>, **Draw near** <note>original: "nagash"</note>, and **Touch** <note>original: "naga"</note>. These three words are sometimes used to describe spatial proximity <note>original: "keravat ha-makom"</note> and the physical attainment of one body touching another. At other times, they are used for proximity in knowledge and in thought, and the attainment of comprehension, as if the object of knowledge has "approached" the one who understands it. 

And sometimes they are used regarding His Providence <term>Providence (Hashgachah): The philosophical concept of God's intervention in or supervision of the universe.</term>, may He be exalted, and the adhesion <note>original: "devikut," a term for spiritual communion or "cleaving" to the Divine</note> of the overflow of powers and prophecy from Him to the prophet. This proximity is called the "Nearness of the Lord," "the Nearness of God," "Divine Providence," and such like. 

Whoever among those who attain [knowledge] feels his soul has approached Him, of him it is said to be a physical attainment—these are the prophets, the pious ones <term>Pious (Chasidim): Those who act with loving-kindness and go beyond the strict requirements of the law to achieve spiritual perfection.</term>, and the supreme holy ones. Along with his connection and proximity to the prophet, there is perfection and a second "seeing," and this shall be sustained by thought. Even if they are hidden, their attainment is perceived by the heart and the [soul]. 

They placed these in the category of the senses to represent the refined proximity between the spiritual beings, the high and the low. For in their very essence and their value within the intellect of God is the Providence appropriate to Him and to the pious man who receives the measures and understands through his intellect the attainment of Providence and the attainments of knowledge and the "intellected" <note>original: "muskal," referring to an object of intellectual perception</note>. And His Providence, as it is, and Wisdom, shall see the spirits as they stir, and they shall know spirit and life. They apply to the bodies of all species, and they are the judged, and the order of its foundation is the Intellect and the Lord.

<meta>This page transitions from the previous discussion on lexicography and mystical definitions (such as "hole" and "incense") into the realm of Jewish civil law (Halakha). Specifically, it explores the mechanics of "Kinyan" (formal acquisition) and "Chalifin" (exchange), moving from the symbolic meaning of words to their practical application in the transfer of property and the resolution of legal disputes in court.</meta>

# 52
If one bought an object and gave another object in its place as an exchange—and both parties are considered buyers—this one has "bought" and this one has "sold," and this one has "bought" and this one has "sold." This process is known as exchange <note>original: חליפין (Chalifin), a legal mechanism where the transfer of one object effects the transfer of another</note>. This can be done with a vessel that has the value of a *perutah* <term>Perutah: the smallest denomination of currency in the Talmud, used as a baseline for legal transactions</term> or even with a vessel that does not have the value of a *perutah*...

# 15
The law is that an act of acquisition can be performed with anything that has the value of a *perutah*, and through it, one acquires from others. For "acquisition" is a formal conduct; the completion of the vessel's transfer "acquires" the property, and only afterward do they formally complete the acquisition. Thus, this person has bought, the acquisition <note>original: קנין (Kinyan)</note> is established, and the matter is awakened. Furthermore, the Sages enacted that one may even use a vessel that does not have the value of a *perutah* <note>a reference to 'Kinyan Sudar', where a simple cloth or item is used to symbolize a contract regardless of its intrinsic value</note>.

## Chapter 13
### Teaching that writing and rhetoric are matters belonging to the holiness of the language

The craft by which one ties many matters together with few words is a profession that follows the "Holiness of the Holy" <note>likely referring to the inner sanctum of the Temple or the highest level of spiritual purity</note> more than anything else a person can grasp through measurement. Other languages can be compared to it, though their words are few and their expressions are muddled; they do not possess this quality. This matter is generally found among actions and those acted upon—this thing exists in their souls exactly as they are, and they are not merely "seated" <note>The author uses the verb "to seat" (*le-hoshiv*), likely continuing the terminology from the previous page's legal discussion to contrast physical placement with spiritual essence</note>. 

I have noted the signs of the rhetoric of the Holy Tongue—those things external to it—so that through their understanding, people will comprehend that all [languages] exist in the world, yet [the Holy Tongue] does not cease from its standing. They do not hear what they themselves are doing and seeing. It is necessary for them to understand that which emerges from the action, for words should not rely solely on their companions. Every "actor" <note>original: *po’el*—can mean both a physical worker and a grammatical verb</note>, except for the One, is an actor through the Choice of the [Prime] Actor. In their eyes, the description and the action are always linked. One who acts from the intellect increases the fruit of writing and integrity. The statement "sending the staff" <note>An idiomatic or scriptural reference to directing authority or influence</note> regarding debt and this change is just as their perceptions might cease before the Master of Masters. Every doubt exists because the matter is found for this necessity; for every leader and manager of the language shows a "friendly face" <note>original: *sever panim*—a welcoming or clear disposition</note> in the action, which is not due to one who lies with his words. Rather, the actor is present in his words, and the brevity of rhetoric is known to his intellect and body.

# The Sanctification of the Name and the Path of Understanding

Sanctify the **Holy Name**; understanding and tranquility are clear. Within the mind and between the wise, his holiness follows an order. The fruit of the **Holy Name** <note>original: *Qodesh HaShem*</note> and His bed shall be established, exempted by goodness to perform all acts of love. He shall find relief and grow wealthy in his desire for the accompaniment he engraved. And with the incense, he shall establish what is taken—as if to say—and he restores glory through it. He is armed for our people, to understand that he will establish with a firm will that which they consider him to know.

The gatekeeper, by the nature of the wall, dwells in strength and is exalted. # Gate Sixteen: The Zeal of One who Prizes Their Soul relative to Others

This gate explores the various types of this spiritual level, including its "counterfeit branch" <note>original: *he-anaf ha-muzayaf*—referring to a false or hypocritical version of a virtue</note> and the obstacles that appear to a person—not just any person, but specifically those in a "good land" <note>likely a metaphor for a person of high moral standing or a favorable environment</note>. It details the superior path of conduct and why a person might desire the qualities of others. In its positive form, this zeal can lead a person to become a hero or a wealthy person <note>spiritually speaking</note> through their own efforts. 

However, the text also warns of the great deficiency this trait can cause, being the root of all "sins of the feet" <note>an idiom for habitual or thoughtless transgressions</note>. It discusses the benefits of reasoning and the management of actions, warning that one must act before the end of their days. 

The "zeal of the one who prizes their soul" occurs when a person thinks it is better to separate themselves so they are not forced into a life of worldly desires. This includes the "wicked envy" toward living people, which contrasts with the desire to acquire wisdom. For the one who knows, the judgment of their will should be guided by the integrity of their intellect, awakening a desire for the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note> and the elevation of the Kingdom.

What is the end for those who sin through these noble traits? They lose even the small benefits of their zeal and youth. Truth must be guarded lest one be forced into a path of weakness. How great is the responsibility!

### The Wise Philosophers and the Definition of Acquiring Character Traits

The **ancient philosophers** <note>original: *hakhmei ha-philosophim ha-kadmonim*—referring to Greek thinkers like Aristotle, whose ethical works heavily influenced Jewish medieval philosophy</note> sought to live a life of the "improved watch," a mission of goodness for the soul. They spoke of how people should strive together, even if the "King of Envy" and other traits like hatred or willpower challenge them. 

To act upon what one knows, one must refine their thoughts through **noble character traits** <note>original: *middot hanechbadot*</note>. The perfection of man <term>Shlemut Ha-Adam (The Perfection of Man): a central concept in Jewish philosophy regarding the ultimate moral and intellectual development of an individual</term> is achieved when the power of the Will is directed toward the most excellent level. These traits should not be subject to random choice; rather, one’s awe regarding them should be holy. These traits of the Lord should be known by every person, guarding against the lowly or diminished traits.

## Chapter 22

Thus shall its boundary be, according to what is fitting and most exceptional and excellent. The boundary of the second level, after the most excellent of the moral virtues, is **Authority** <term>Ha-Misrah: leadership, dominion, or the holding of public office</term>. This is the most excellent state, involving the desire of the upright leader or the motivator who chooses this path; he is not relegated to the level of a mere hireling <note>original: *mechir*, literally "price," suggesting one who works only for reward</note>. However, this name and the "Authority" mentioned here refers to one who—though perhaps weak in the most excellent matters of the speaking faculty—inclines toward what appears to him to be good. This is the definition of the virtue of Authority. Indeed, the perfect, universal leader is not truly found, except for **Moses our Teacher** <note>original: *Moshe Rabbeinu*, peace be upon him</note> and the other great sages of the nation. This mandatory Authority should be joined with this virtue, that he may lead and sustain the entire nation and expand its borders. 

One who truly contemplates the matter of laws will find nothing better for humanity than those meant to order the **perfect community** <note>original: *ha-kehillah ha-shelemah*; an echo of the "Ideal City" or "Polis" in political philosophy</note> from an elevated perspective. Authority is divided into various parts... and the correct matter, accepted by those who contemplate with the **eyes of the heart** <note>A mystical/philosophical term for intuitive or spiritual perception</note>, is perhaps that these things are proven through the law of **free choice** <note>original: *mishpat ha-bechirah*</note>, the choice of the mistress <note>likely a metaphor for the intellect ruling over the physical faculties</note>, and the enduring reality.

# The Holy of Holies regarding the fulfillment of the commandments dependent on the sanctification of the Blessed Name and <unclear>...</unclear>

And it is the second commandment to be counted in the enumeration of the commandments according to the opinion of the Rabbi, Rabbi Moses son of Maimon <note>original: "Moshe bar Maimon," the 12th-century scholar known as Maimonides or Rambam</note>, of blessed memory, in the *Book of Commandments* and in the *Book of Knowledge* within the *Laws of the Foundations of the Torah*. And he completed them together in twenty-five chapters.

**The first chapter** concerning "Dispositions" <term>Dispositions|Hebrew: De’ot; refers to ethical character traits, temperaments, and psychological health</term> will be explained, along with the conduct of the body and the excellence of character traits, and the levels by which a person should conduct himself with other people. It makes known the matter of character traits that follow the traits of the Creator, may His name be blessed, and that the ultimate human desire is to resemble Him, may His name be blessed, and its measure.

**Chapter 14** establishes it in the kingdom of the Lordship that exists before Him, may He be blessed, in the sanctification of the Holy Names, to make known that every aspect has a name testifying to sanctity and eminence.

**Chapter 15** mentions the laws of all things holy. <margin>20</margin> Within it, he explains the "right hand of God" which maintains His loving-kindness with every living thing; He does not remove His kindness from them. This is the foundation upon which His place of worship stands. In it, one discerns what is pure and holy, where there is no profanation, so as not to cast away anything from the holy, and the spirit of the One sanctified to Him which is within us—this is the matter of the "Holy of Holies" in the traditional way.

**Chapter 16** mentions the name *Elohim* <note>original: "Elohim," a Divine name often associated in Jewish thought with Justice and the laws of nature</note>—Judgment and Might. It is sustained according to the order of custom, with fixed retribution and fixed reward. From these come branches and their foundation, and the entire existence of human beings and their standing is within this.

**Chapter 17** mentions the three levels of prophecy in which human perceptions are divided. Some are through the perceived intellect, some through the perceived with intellectual imagination, and some through the perceived imagination. Known in my heart is the matter and the ultimate perfection, and the level of the angels called "Universal" <note>likely referring to the 'Common Sense' or 'Universal Mind' in medieval philosophy</note> within the heart grasped by the intellect.

**Chapter 18** mentions the payment of the reward hidden for the righteous, and the psychic portion of the soul. This is the secret of the "dispute" <note>likely referring to the rabbinic debates regarding the nature of the World to Come</note> that our Sages of blessed memory taught. It also addresses the matter of the completely wicked person who destroys his body and soul and becomes as if he never was. It explains the laws of the primordial reward in this, and the explanation of the "Supreme Speaker" which he mentions throughout.

<meta>While the previous page focused on the prophetic visions of Ezekiel and the spiritual conditions of the Babylonian exile, this page shifts toward a scientific and philosophical inquiry. It reconciles traditional Rabbinic identifications of the stars with the astronomical knowledge of the Greeks and Chaldeans, ultimately arguing that the Sages' words should be understood as allegorical riddles rather than literal descriptions.</meta>

The ancients wrote that within the two legs of the **Great Bear** <note>Ursa Major</note> are 
**Kesil** <note>original: "כסיל" - identified as the constellation Orion</note> and **Ash** <note>original: "עש" - often identified as the Pleiades or Arcturus</note>. This was also written by the **Radak** <term>Radak|Rabbi David Kimhi (1160–1235), a preeminent medieval Jewish commentator and grammarian</term> in the Talmudic tractate *Chullin*, in the chapter "The Covering of the Blood." 

And this is his language: "According to the little I have seen in their books, the west of the Bear [contains] the legs of the **Bull** <note>Taurus</note>; and behold, they are well-known and famous. The ancient **Greeks** and **Chaldeans** <term>Chaldeans|An ancient people of Mesopotamia renowned for their early mastery of astronomy and astrology</term> call it 'the Bull,' and they said they saw two stars that were called the **Eye of the Bull** <note>The star Aldebaran</note>," etc.

Behold, after I have written all this, and investigated and inquired from the mouths of the enlightened and the wise men of all the nations found in this land, I saw that all of them together did not speak correctly. The names famous in the books of the astronomers are different from these three mentioned in **The Duties of the Heart** <term>Chovot HaLevavot|A classic 11th-century work of Jewish philosophy by Bahya ibn Paquda</term> and others. It is fitting for every wise and enlightened man to investigate and expand upon this. 

However, this essay, in its writing, is a narrative—a parable of the examination. For this speech, the metaphor that appears in the words of the Sages, seems like a false dream or like words that are hard and heavy in the eyes of men; for they see them [the words] as if all their time passes without order. Therefore, the Sages, may their memory be a blessing, said etc. 

And as for those who respond to their words: the Sages, may their memory be a blessing, said that because their words are entirely riddles and secrets, I have not truly heard [understood] them. Furthermore, their holy words are not for their own sake, but for the sake of the recipient. And regarding the speech—it is not that the matter is [only] precious, nor is it harmful; on the contrary, the recipients are the ones who are delayed, even though they were ancient men. For their words are words of riddles. 

There is an old parable of a man who enters a **goldsmith's shop**: he sees this vessel of gold and thinks, "There is much gold here." Sometimes people perceive both gold and copper in the goldsmith's shop, or regarding all shops and merchandise. All that the ancients have in their "shop" are straightforward things, both understandable and deep, which the Sages found at that time. 

Therefore, they called him the "Master of Parables," after the parables known as *Kahana* <note>Possibly referring to the Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, a collection of midrashic homilies</note>. The things spoken by our mouths and in the **Chronicles** <note>original: "דברי הימים" - likely referring to the biblical book or historical records</note> are part of those matters; for their words were not said in their plain, literal sense, but rather as parables and metaphors—"the words of the wise and their riddles."

<summary>This page discusses the identification of biblical constellations like Orion and the Pleiades, comparing Rabbinic tradition with Greek and Chaldean astronomy. It concludes by arguing that the Sages' teachings are often allegorical "riddles" that require deep interpretation rather than a literal reading.</summary>

Behold, we have already explained and supported this by that which is found in the Midrash of our Sages <note>original: "Rizal" - Rabbis of Blessed Memory</note> on the verse: 
"And thus his mother said to him, to Lemuel: Do not give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which destroys kings." <note>Proverbs 31:1-3; Lemuel is traditionally identified by the Sages as King Solomon. The "mother" is interpreted as Bathsheba giving moral instruction.</note> 
Wealth does not profit in the bundle of wisdom. However, because we are running lest we be overtaken in our smallness—for we were accustomed to the habits of fools on the day of the covenant—a portion has come to be our lot and our acquisition: the <term>Sextus|The 'Liber Sextus', a collection of Catholic Canon law added to the Decretals in 1298</term> and the <term>Decretals|The 'Decretales', the primary authoritative collection of medieval Church law</term>. By elevating status and name and "good law," they appear close to what is popular but are actually very far from the way of truth.

And their response to them concerning their thoughts about us, as they say: "Of what use are the <term>Sextus</term> and <term>Decretals</term> and the words of the ancients?" # On the Nature of Essential Holiness

There is a concept of **essential holiness** <note>original: "Kedushah Atzmah"</note> itself, and everything written upon it must be directed by the scribe’s intent; otherwise, the writing is considered blank and invalid. Similarly, the matter of the **Curtain** <term>Parochet; the heavy tapestry that separated the Holy of Holies from the rest of the Tabernacle</term> of the **Tabernacle** <term>Mishkan; the portable earthly dwelling place of God during the Exodus</term> derives its holiness from its function as a partition, and there is no doubt in this.

There is the Curtain, and then there is the **Ark-Cover** <term>Kapporet; the golden lid placed atop the Ark of the Covenant</term>. The holiness of the cover of the Ark <note>original: "Teiva," meaning chest or box</note> resides in its role as a covering for the sake of the atonement-piece. The holiness of the **surrounding layer** <note>original: "Makif"; a kabbalistic concept referring to a light or holiness that encompasses an object from without</note> exists due to the "edge," which rests upon the inner libation and upon the Curtain. 

Following this logic, the holiness of the **Priestly Garments** <note>the vestments worn by the Kohanim</note> stems from their status as that which "surrounds" the body. They are not merely "changes of clothes," for the holiness of many sacred things resides in their capacity as a surrounding layer.

There is a specific intention in my knowledge—and "they were finished" <note>original: "Vayechulu"; a reference to Genesis 2:1, "And the heavens and the earth were finished"</note>—I knew it was not merely a holy branch. This relates to the **Tablets of the Covenant**. The script was written upon the Ark, upon the inner tablet, so that the name of the Tablets would be upon them. All of this is so that the blessings and the families may return to them, for they are the **conduits** <term>Tzinorot; spiritual pipes or channels through which divine abundance flows into the world</term> that flow from below and from above.

It appears that the Names <note>the Holy Names of God</note> written within a book do not possess internal holiness solely for the sake of what is written as "holy" or "sanctified." According to this, the "Holy" becomes the glory returned to the blessings. 

However, it seemed to me, through the mercies of the **Creator**, that to the observer, the logic is twofold. Even when regarding the sight of His deeds (may He be blessed), if a portion of it surrounds the heart and the senses within the scope of one's ability, one should not say explicitly that it is merely "Nature." Through the nullification of his own soul and will, a person shall not sin by approaching it as something secular <note>original: "Chul"</note>; rather, he should approach it in the name of the Torah. The sight is an "exceeding of Nature," which guides these actions. The incense-smoke was a statute from above; they did not perform it in isolation but through the order of holiness, even if it involved a change or a nullification of the self.

This concerns the judgment of **Custom** <term>Minhag; traditional practice</term> and the leadership of small matters, for even the will of the Scripture conducts itself and is not separated from it. This pertains to its being, its existence, its life, and its power. To establish them, one cannot detail every specific, such as the "external general rule." And it was not in the "Land of the Living" <note>a poetic term for the Land of Israel or the spiritual realm</note> that the holiness of the pillars was established in such a way.

And in its **essence** <note>original: "dhat" - the core reality or self of a thing</note>, rather by the very right of its essence. As for what is found in the **innate nature** <note>original: "fitra" - the natural, God-given disposition of a human being</note>, in this there is a difference regarding what is composed and that which exists in its essence. As for that which is known through the **intellect** <note>original: "al-aql" - the rational faculty that perceives universal truths</note>, it is not built upon individual essences. The meaning known through action is what we mentioned regarding its essence. As for the rest of the convention regarding what is known in the essence, it contains the <term>definition</term> <note>original: "al-hadd" - the formal logical statement of what a thing is</note> which is something else entirely.

Convention is what is composed, and it does not reside in the essence itself; rather, it exists in the soul by way of convention. As for what resides truly in the essence, the <term>definition</term> is the intellect. Convention, regarding the essence, is merely the <term>meaning</term>, which is the truth within the essence; however, there is no certainty found in it according to common convention. This is the **form** <note>original: "al-sura" - the Aristotelian concept of 'form' that gives matter its identity</note> of the essence, and this is distinct from the essence itself. 

That which is known in the essence regarding the cause is distinct from the essences. For nothing external falls into the essence of the "known" itself; at that point, it is the essence. As for the <term>meaning</term> that remains in its essence, it is the <term>definition</term> in its essence, and it exists in the soul by convention. Thus, the essence contains the <term>definition</term> within it. The form that exists in its essence is the truth in the essence among the essences.

The <term>meaning</term> exists in its essence by the definition in the essence. As for that which is the **intellect**, the essence within it exists in the soul. **Perfection** <note>original: "al-kamal" - the state of being complete or reaching one's purpose</note> in the essence exists in the soul by convention. Thus, the meaning in the essence is the truth in the essence regarding the cause. That which was in the soul is the truth.

After he gave one or half a *kortov* for this, an hour in the evening and after the *kav* of these *kurtis*, behold it is a *kav* per year before ascending to the plain. At that time it continued and is not lacking the expense, and there is a deficiency of a *kav* from the length.

The reason and the principle appear to be because a *kav* per year and half a *kav* per year seem to be a fine conclusion for the food that the merchant gave. The *kortisa* of a *kav* per year is given once, lest any deficiency be felt, so as to remain secure in a great deed. He calculated a similar sign, such as the measurement of the deficiency of the one delivering the goods, which adds to the deficiency: half a *kav* is lacking within the *sa'in* <term>sa'in: the plural of "sa'ah," a dry measure equal to six kavs</term> of wheat, and the remainder is lacking within the *sa'in*.

The heavens, etc. It is a well-known fact that movement, sound, and all "accidents" <term>accidents: in medieval philosophy, these are properties like color or sound that cannot exist on their own but must belong to a physical substance</term> cannot possess the stability to exist separately by themselves. They have no standing except through a recipient <note>original: *mekabel*</note> that sustains them, much like wax or water which receives the form of a seal; they hold that form through the strength of their own stability, according to the power of the recipient over them. If there were no sustainer present to stand between them, everything would go to ruin and become like smoke burned away before the sun, or like wax dissolved by fire. Regarding the "small attributes" <note>this likely refers to the lower or more limited emotional states of the soul</note> and that which seemed to them as not being able to sustain anything—these would become as nothing. They would have no hope of strength or of upholding the holiness built within them.

The hidden attributes are unable to endure the intensity of holiness on their own. Therefore, it is said of them, "the Matrons" <note>original: *Matronot*; a term often used for the feminine aspect of Divine Presence or high-ranking angelic forces</note> and the "Seraphim" <term>Seraphim: "the burning ones," a high order of angels associated with fire and the purification of the soul</term>, and the "nullification" and "perishing" within the intensity of the Holy Inner Light. This serves to demonstrate that one must not walk improperly in the ways of holiness. To ensure the listener understands this, it is said that the Divine has placed separations at the points where the lights are divided among all parts of the attributes and the "extremities" <note>the six directional points of the spiritual universe</note>. This is to show the distinction between "Being" <term>Yesh: manifest, tangible existence</term> and "Nothingness" <term>Ayin: the primordial, infinite source from which all begins</term> within every creature and their boundary. Thus, there is a stability for all parts of holiness so they do not intermingle with one another, and also to demonstrate this principle.

It is known that there is no waiving of Divine Judgment <note>original: *ein vitur b'din*; a Rabbinic principle suggesting that God’s justice is precise and cannot be simply ignored or bypassed</note>; however, through forgiveness, a portion of the aforementioned decree may be pardoned. ## Chapter 9: The Will that Moves the Power; The General Secret, The First Offering

The movement and the action of a human being—even among the various **classes** <term>Kitot: categories or groups, referring here to the different faculties of the soul</term>—arise from the **Natural, Vital, and Intellectual** <term>Tiv'iyot, Hiyuniyot, Sikhliyot: the three standard divisions of the soul in medieval philosophy—the vegetative, animal, and rational levels</term> faculties. Within these, actions are divided into their respective levels according to their value. Though all are equal in being either complete or lacking, nature is arranged according to these levels in relation to human power.

This remains true whether one is in a state of confusion or is **free** <term>hofshi: referring to the exercise of free will</term>, and whether one seeks to acquire the habit of action or suffers from human deficiency. It applies whether one seeks to do the good, or to "bind the bonds" <note>This may refer to theurgy or the binding of spiritual forces common in Kabbalistic literature</note>, or whether the "Prince" who speaks <term>Ha-Medaber: the rational or speaking soul</term> achieves its purpose. Indeed, this is the **Acquired Intellect** <term>Sekhel Ha-Nikneh: the highest level of human intellect, where the mind has actualized its potential and joined with the universal Active Intellect</term>, which becomes nature itself.

Whether it is a matter of having trust, or calling upon the **Blessed One** <term>Ha-Shem Yitbarakh: "The Blessed Name," a common pious way to refer to God</term>—because of whom a chance event occurred while the man hears and remains silent—or whether one blesses by the power of the Name, or understands a book, or performs a kindness through **Rectifications** <term>Tikkunim: spiritual repairs or ritual acts intended to restore cosmic balance</term> (even if not for their own sake or for the sake of the Name itself), or if it is an act of pure kindness, truth, or justice—human **Will** <term>Ratzon: the driving desire or intention</term> directs it.

This is the end of the matter: whatever occurs passes over everything, while one remains silent and guards eternal justice and truth. I sought help from the **Blessed Name** and began to understand these things: whether to examine all the "vessels" <note>In this context, "vessels" likely refers to the human faculties or the spiritual instruments used in divine service</note> with the assumption of what is to come, or for a single individual alone and the reason for it, or to add the name of their owner. According to the measure of kindness, it shall be said to all: "receive the aforementioned power." Their perfection, their names, and the divisions of their leadership shall be calculated. And to the righteous man, it shall be said: "to all life!" Thus, there shall be a "hand of peace." The reason for this account is that every aspect is known through the conduct of the **Celestial Sphere** <term>Galgal: the revolving heavens or cosmic cycles</term> and the foundation of the vessel; therefore, the reason for establishing their secrets is clear.

Just as those who bring a **burnt offering** <term>Korban Olah: a "rising" sacrifice entirely consumed by fire, symbolizing total devotion</term> as a memorial before the Lord, so too is all the merit of Israel and their ancestors brought forward. May He return to support us; God is good in His kindness, supporting the soul toward our God.
